speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked 	the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry has done any study to ascertain the impact of a disposable carrier bag charge on vulnerable households, especially the elderly; (b) how will such a charge impact residents who use such bags to dispose of their daily household waste in HDB flats; (c) how will the charge apply to home deliveries from supermarkets; and (d) whether supermarket employees, including those who pack groceries for deliveries, receive training to use minimal packaging.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the current global economic crisis, whether the Ministry will (i) consider deferring the implementation of the charging model for disposable carrier bags and (ii) assess the potential impact of such additional charges on the lower income groups.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry plans to allow only the use of biodegradable plastic bags to replace the current plastic bags; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider incentivising the use of such biodegradable bags to balance the need of residents to bag their trash before they are disposed into common rubbish chutes in our high-rise environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) when will the Ministry complete the public consultation on developing an appropriate disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets; (b) what measures is the Ministry considering to take to lower the impact of this charge on lower income families; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider charging per bag from the third bag and providing lower income families with a reusable shopping bag each.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Excessive consumption of disposables is unsustainable and can be avoided if all stakeholders work together to change mindsets, habits and behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Implementing a charge for single-use carrier bags at supermarkets is one of the recommendations submitted by the Citizens' Workgroup on Reducing the Excessive Consumption of Disposables to change social behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many jurisdictions overseas have already implemented disposable carrier bag charges with positive results.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: A disposable carrier bag charge is not new to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of the Plastic ACTion business initiative started by World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) Singapore, retailers such as Uniqlo, Watsons, H&M and The Body Shop have committed to a bag charge and collectively achieved over 60% reduction in single-use bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NTUC FairPrice has also piloted bag charges and received positive response.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In developing an appropriate model for a disposable carrier bag charge at supermarkets, the National Environment Agency (NEA) will study overseas examples and consult key stakeholders and members of the public.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, the amount to be charged; whether the charge will apply per transaction, or per bag from the first or third bag; implementation timeline; and how the charge proceeds will be used.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will take into account our local context, such as the current practice of reusing disposable carrier bags to bag rubbish for disposal.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will also look into any possible impact of a charge, especially on the more vulnerable groups such as low-income households, and will consult MSF and social service agencies on the possible mitigation measures to address the impact.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Plastic waste generated in Singapore is either recycled or sent to our waste-to-energy plants for incineration and not landfilled directly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the environmental benefits of using biodegradable plastic bags do not apply in Singapore, we have no plans to encourage their use over conventional plastic bags.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Every type of packaging material results in different environmental impacts such as carbon emissions and water consumption.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Rather than substituting plastic disposables with disposables made of other materials such as biodegradable plastics, the more sustainable approach is to reduce the excessive use of disposables altogether.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The disposable carrier bag charge is intended to discourage the excessive use of disposable bags and to promote the use of reusables.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, this measure alone is not a silver bullet.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We must address this issue on multiple fronts, from enhancing public education and awareness, to behavioural nudges, to working with producers and retailers to use less packaging upstream.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All of us must play our part to catalyse a mindset and behavioural shift towards a greener and zero-waste Singapore.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Louis Ng, may I ask for your clarification to be kept short.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, in jurisdictions like Hong Kong and Taiwan, they do take a phased approach too.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: What is going to be the impact on the average household?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Instead of charging for plastic bag usage, whether the Ministry has considered and explored incentivising "Bring Your Own Bag" initiative instead.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to do this on multiple fronts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, NEA has supported, say, Zero Waste SG, for instance, in their initiative to reach out to F&B and other retailers to incentivise people to bring their own reusable containers and bags.
